set.approach: Hike the 50 Year Trail and watch to the right for a pair of large boulders sitting on a rocky hilltop. A fence has to be ducked under for the brief off-trail stretch to the climbs. Scramble up to the start of the route from the right.

review.notes: Area page: approach and fence; route page: scramble up from the right. No descent stated.

set.approach: Follow the dirt roads east onto the Middle Gate Trail, then cross the wash and climb. Make for the ridge, walk south along it to the hilltop, and continue until you can drop onto the slab. Dirty Psy is the first route on the left and shares its chain anchor with the route to its right.

review.notes: Area page: approach; route page: first route on the left, shared anchor. No descent stated.

set.approach: Follow the dirt roads east onto the Middle Gate Trail, then cross the wash and climb. Make for the ridge, walk south along it to the hilltop, and continue until you can drop onto the slab. We were here first is the longest route on the rock, bolted up the middle of the face on a thin low-angle slab.

review.notes: Area page: approach; route page: longest route, middle of the face. No descent stated.

set.approach: Stay on the 50 Year Trail, which passes this boulder on the right about halfway to Catalina Dome. The steep seam splitting the boulder on the trail side catches the eye. Hey Joe is the bolted route on the sunny side, and it gains the summit of the boulder, where bolts also allow top-roping.

review.notes: Area page: trail and boulder; route page: right off the trail, bolted summit. No descent stated.

set.approach: The McNutt climbing area is BLM land along the northern edge of the wilderness, entered through a gate. From the parking area the walls are a short walk up the wash. Notorious Wall is the first area reachable from the parking lot: walk south from the parking area to where the wash changes from a north-south to an east-west course, and use the burro trail alongside the wash. The route climbs a spring runoff at the end of the wall, and the belay is a small cave. Party and Bullshit is the next line along.

review.notes: Area pages: gate, wash and burro trail; route page: spring runoff, cave belay. East/west placement left out because the page contradicts itself. No descent stated.

set.approach: The McNutt climbing area is BLM land along the northern edge of the wilderness, entered through a gate. From the parking area the walls are a short walk up the wash. Wu Tang Wall is reached from roughly the midpoint of the access road beyond the gate: go west off the road, cross the riverbed, and climb to the freestanding wall.
